title: PRD: Client-side Traffic Shaping, Local Replay & Deterministic Pagination Debug Hooks (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Deliver a client-side feature set across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that enables: 1) deterministic traffic shaping and soft-throttling controls to reduce server-side overload; 2) an embeddable local-replay tool that captures paginated/streaming sessions for deterministic debugging; and 3) deterministic pagination debug hooks (cursor snapshots, request/response replay) to reproduce and triage edge-case failures without changing server behavior.
background: Customer support and platform engineering have seen a rise in hard-to-reproduce pagination and streaming issues that only happen under specific client sequencing, intermittent retries, or bursty traffic. Existing server-side logs are insufficient to reconstruct the client-side sequence (ordering of retries, backoffs, and partial stream reads). We need SDK-level instrumentation and optional local replay to allow engineers to reproduce problems deterministically in CI or locally and to apply traffic shaping to avoid customer-facing outages.
goals: Expose a small set of client-side knobs to control rate shaping (max-inflight, token-bucket burst, adaptive backoff) with sane defaults per language
Provide a lightweight, opt-in local-replay artifact (JSONL) that records request/response streams, cursor snapshots and retry decisions, and can be replayed against a mocked server or a local proxy
Add deterministic pagination debug hooks that capture KV-cache state, last-successful-cursor, and per-request metadata for reproducible bug reports
Ensure feature parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and a consistent developer experience for generating and consuming replay artifacts
Design APIs that are forward-compatible with planned runtime features (server-driven throttling and model fallbacks)
non_goals: Server-side replay or storage of full customer request traces (out of scope for SDK deliverable)
Making replay artifacts mandatory or collected by default (must remain opt-in and privacy-safe)
Full end-to-end capture of PII-sensitive fields (SDK will provide redaction hooks but will not default-capture sensitive data)
proposed_api_contracts: Python: ClientTrafficManager(max_inflight=4, burst=8, adapt=True, policy="exponential+-jitter") contextmanager; ReplayRecorder(path) start()/stop(); replay.Playback(path, server_mock_url)

TypeScript: new TrafficShaper({maxInflight:4, burst:8, adaptive:true}); const recorder = new ReplayRecorder('./replays/session-202603.jsonl'); await recorder.start(); await client.paginate(...); await recorder.stop();
Go: type Shaper struct{MaxInflight int; Burst int; Policy string}; func NewShaper(...) *Shaper; recorder := replay.NewRecorder(io.Writer); recorder.Record(reqMeta, respChunk, cursorSnapshot)
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose traffic shaping API and defaults are documented; unit tests demonstrate throttling under synthetic loads
Local-replay artifact format defined (JSONL spec) and roundtrips: recorder -> playback -> equivalent sequence of server-side events in a local mock
Deterministic pagination hook installed: ability to snapshot cursor state and replay to reach same cursor and reproduce a failing response deterministically in >= 3 sample bugs
E2E test: inject transient 503s in a paginated stream; SDK replay reproduces the identical retry sequence and final error seen in production logs
Docs: PRD+implementation guide and migration notes published in Confluence; quickstart examples for Python/TS/Go in SDK repo docs
Security: replay artifacts must include a redaction pipeline; CI check validates no secrets land in example replays
Compatibility: existing public SDK surface remains backward-compatible; new traffic shaping is optional and disabled by default
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Replays could inadvertently capture secrets. Mitigation: default redaction, explicit opt-in, and CI linter to reject artifacts containing obvious tokens
Risk: Divergence between language SDKs causing mismatch in reproduction. Mitigation: shared JSONL schema and cross-language replay unit tests
Risk: Added complexity to SDK surface might confuse users. Mitigation: keep top-level API minimal, expose advanced controls behind "advanced" module
Risk: Traffic shaping could cause unexpected latency increases. Mitigation: performance benchmarks and guardrail values in defaults
updates: 2026-03-05: Created PRD draft; initial scoping session with SDK and runtime teams. Recorded follow-ups: define JSONL schema and redaction fields.
2026-03-07: Engineering review notes (Chen Li): prefer token-bucket implementation in runtime for stricter guarantees; agreed to keep client-side opt-in shaper for best-effort avoidance of overload.
2026-03-09: UX feedback (Docs): provide one-line quickstart snippets for all three languages and link to playground replay tool. Action: Mateo to prototype recorder API for Python by 2026-03-19.
2026-03-12: Security review kickoff: Priya requested explicit consent language and retention TTL for replay files. Added acceptance criterion for CI redaction checks.
notes: Prototype CLI tool suggested: rw-sdk-replay serve --mock --from ./session.jsonl to allow QA to quickly spin up a mock server that replays recorded sessions
Consider adding a small visualizer for replay timeline in Console as a later phase (post-MVP)
Estimate assumes one full cross-lang parity sprint and a follow-up sprint for docs + e2e tests
